title: Separate Student t scale fits gave no clear six-month ENSO density score gain at 1981-2024 origins
abstract: We tested separate Student t scale fits for six-month ENSO probability forecasts. We reused a fixed NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 snapshot, earlier-only forecast means and 528 monthly origins in 1981-2024. The seasonal scale was fitted by each distribution's own likelihood. Normal-minus-fitted-t5 density score gain was -0.01353 nats, with conditional 95% three-year block limits of -0.03136 to +0.00624. Five- and ten-year limits also included zero. Separate t5 fitting reduced point loss against an equal-variance t5 control but gave no clear gain over the normal rule. Its nominal 98% intervals covered 99.62% of outcomes and were 26.2% wider than normal intervals. Interval-score gains were uncertain. This extends prior campaign work on the same data. Fixed symmetric tails, one revised product, dependent cycles and conditional intervals limit inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate evidence, checks and a figure are included. Source records remain external.

display.caption: Annual primary density score gain, conditional 95% limits for all fixed rules, and interval coverage. Positive gains favor Student errors. The primary fitted t5 interval crosses zero.

citations.reason: We reuse the mean model, exact input, forecast dates and baseline-licensed code. We test its stated scale-fitting limitation. Observations overlap.
